# Switch NX2 - read when the Lichii GUI starts.
# One NAME=VALUE per line. Lines starting with # are ignored.
# A variable already set in the environment wins over this file.
# Between files, the user copy (%APPDATA%\eden\nx2_switches.txt, or
# $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/eden/nx2_switches.txt) wins over this one, so editing this file is never
# needed: copy the lines you want into your own and restart.
#
# Restart the emulator after editing.

# --- Performance tuning defaults for Switch 2 ---
# Offload GPU method/macro execution to the back thread (SPLIT=2 delivers up to +54% FPS alone).
EDEN_NX2_SPLIT=2

# Batch GPU fence syncpoints to reduce host driver overhead and smooth frametimes.
EDEN_NX2_FENCE_BATCH=1

# Leave buffer downloads disabled on Switch 2 (default): forcing downloads (=1) copies back
# 90-220 MB/s of buffers CPU never touches, causing heavy mutex contention and dropping FPS by ~38-63%.
#EDEN_NX2_BUFFER_DOWNLOADS=1

# Paces frame submission 2 frames ahead. Reduces frametime spikes, but adds ~1-2 frames of input latency.
# Enable only if frame pacing stability is preferred over responsive controls.
#EDEN_NX2_FRAMES_AHEAD=2

# --- Workarounds / Debug ---
# Terrain/indirect drawing fix for Donkey Kong Bananza: enabled by default. Set to 0 only to leave to GPU.
#EDEN_NX2_RESETFIX=0

# Drop reactive-flushing read traps on Switch 2 programs (opt-in; can reduce FPS from 29 to 24 in MKW).
#EDEN_NX2_NO_REACTIVE=1

# Graphics pipelines linked from per-stage shader libraries (VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library with
# fast linking; not on MoltenVK). Off by default; EDEN_NX2_GPL_FAST_LINK=0 links optimized.
#EDEN_NX2_GPL=1

# With EDEN_NX2_GPL=1 and "Precache shaders before game start": the game's vertex and fragment
# programs are also prepared (rebuild the precache after setting it). Ocarina of Time: a 1.5 GB
# file, six more minutes on the first loading screen, 2.3 GB of driver cache; pop-in ends sooner,
# frame times are the same as with the compute precache alone.
#EDEN_NX2_GRAPHICS_PRECACHE=1

# Ocarina of Time with the "AMD FSR 3.1" anti-aliasing choice: 0 draws the scene without the
# per-frame sub-pixel offset FSR is given.
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_JITTER=0

# Ocarina of Time with NVIDIA DLSS (or MetalFX temporal): 1 gives it the same sub-pixel offset,
# 2 with the vertical sign flipped. Experiment, off by default.
#EDEN_NX2_DLSS_JITTER=1

# Ocarina of Time: 1 draws the game's upscale pass as one bilinear tap whenever no temporal
# upscaler takes the frame (phones get it from their device profile; 0 turns it off there).
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_BILINEAR_UPSCALE=1

# Ocarina of Time handheld: 1 lets DLSS / FSR 3.1 take the upscale from the lower scales to
# 1920x1080 (on by default on Apple for MetalFX temporal, 0 turns it off).
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_TEMPORAL_HANDHELD=1

# A draw without render targets (it writes buffers or counts samples only) gets a render pass as
# large as its scissors reach instead of the surface clip (Ocarina of Time leaves that at
# 32768x32768). On by default on Apple, where the GPU prepares every tile of it; 0 turns it off.
#EDEN_NX2_TARGETLESS_REACH=1

# Streamed uniform buffers on MoltenVK: static (default) pads to the shader's used size unless it
# indexes the buffer; readable also zero-fills indexed ones to 64 KiB, bank always 64 KiB, poison
# fills with 0xff the shader can see (finds reads past the guest's size), 0 none.
#EDEN_NX2_UBO_PAD=static

# 0: a fence release submits deferred GPU work only when its callback has not run (something
# waits). Phones get 0 from their device profile.
#EDEN_NX2_RELEASE_SUBMIT=1

# The split GPU thread, out of commands with a deferred submission younger than
# EDEN_NX2_FENCE_FLUSH_US, waits up to this many us for more work first (it spins meanwhile).
#EDEN_NX2_IDLE_GRACE_US=0

# The fencing thread lets a deferred fence submission wait this many us after the fence was
# made before it asks the GPU thread for it (0 = at once).
#EDEN_NX2_FENCE_PATIENCE_US=0

# An emulated mesh draw inside a render pass that began on a command buffer of its own runs its
# compute just before that pass instead of ending and reopening it (when no draw of the pass stored
# to memory and it samples none of the pass's targets). 0 ends the pass as before.
#EDEN_NX2_MESH_BEFORE_PASS=1

# MoltenVK: a guest dispatch right after another one (only bindings between) records no barrier,
# so both share one serial Metal compute encoder (a barrier ends it). Off by default; force applies
# it on every driver, for tests only (not valid Vulkan).
#EDEN_NX2_DISPATCH_CHAIN=1

# Mesh pipelines the driver could build natively take the compute emulation instead: all, or a
# comma list of pipeline hashes. To compare the two (Apple mesh shaders are occupancy bound).
#EDEN_NX2_MESH_EMULATE=all

#EDEN_NX2_MME_JIT=0
#EDEN_NX2_PBFLUSH=0
#EDEN_NX2_SKIP_SAME=0
#EDEN_NX2_INLINE_DEFER=0
#EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_SKIP=1
#EDEN_NX2_AUTO_STUB=1
#EDEN_NX2_KEEP_ASTC=1

# --- Memory ---
# Windows: guest memory is committed as the game allocates it instead of all at start (about
# 4.5 GiB less commit charge in Ocarina of Time). Set to 0 to commit all of it at start.
#EDEN_NX2_SEC_RESERVE=0

# Cap the texture cache's device memory (MiB) below what the graphics driver's budget allows.
#EDEN_NX2_TC_CEILING_MIB=7680

# --- CPU scheduling ---
# Hex mask of guest cores whose host threads keep the top priority (and on Apple the performance
# cores); the others run one class lower. On a 4-CPU host (2 fast + 2 slow, no pinning) Kokiri
# Forest went from 52-53 to 66-70 fps with 03; no change with all 24 CPUs.
#EDEN_NX2_GUEST_CORE_FIRST=03

# Ocarina of Time: 0 keeps the game's own multi-core masks, 2 narrows each to the thread's ideal
# core (default: widened to every core).
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_WIDE_AFFINITY=0

# Yield backoff: a gap between two yields longer than this (us, default 100) starts a new run;
# with 0, changed callee-saved registers no longer start one. Ocarina of Time changes them at
# every yield, so its backoff never sleeps; making it sleep cost about 60 % of the frame rate.
#EDEN_NX2_YIELD_BACKOFF_GAP_US=100
#EDEN_NX2_YIELD_BACKOFF_REGS=0

# "Perf sched:" line (with EDEN_NX2_PERF_REPORT=1): list the busiest n guest threads (default 5).
#EDEN_NX2_PERF_SCHED_THREADS=5
# 0 drops the "Perf threads:" and "Perf sched:" lines and the counting behind them.
#EDEN_NX2_PERF_SCHED=0

# Guest loads/stores that take the JIT's memory callbacks ("Perf memory callbacks:" line).
# arm64 hosts: 1 runs LDXR/STXR in fastmem (a load and a host CAS) instead of a callback each
# (off by default: Ocarina of Time runs none on the PC; iOS Experiments turns it on).
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_INLINE_EXCLUSIVES=1
# A plain load that faults in fastmem gives fastmem up only at its nth fault (default 0 or 1: at
# the first). Read traps fault once and are then disarmed; on the PC phone sim 8 cut Ocarina of
# Time's GPU-tracked slow loads 14k -> 4k/s, but those left are the flushing reads.
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_LOAD_FAULTS=8
# x64, diagnostic: 1 sends LDXR/STXR through the callbacks and the global monitor, as arm64 did.
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_EXCLUSIVE_CALLBACKS=1
# The reactive flushing setting for this session (0 = read traps, as on iOS and macOS).
#EDEN_NX2_REACTIVE_FLUSHING=0
